body: SYDNEY, Australia — Pill testing spaces will be a permanent fixture at music festivals in New South Wales, the most populated state in Australia, after a trial was found to reduce drug‑related harm. The NSW government this week confirmed festival-goers would have access to free, anonymous drug testing services, which would roll out at up to 15 events statewide each year. title: UGREEN’s smart home hubs put an AI data center in your kitchen to protect your privacy
summary: Putting privacy on a pedestal — if you can afford it.
body: TL;DR UGREEN is launching three smart home hubs that combine network storage, video recording, and local AI processing. Instead of talking to Gemini in the cloud like you do with Google Home, here all voice commands are processed by the hub itself. Depending on your needs, UGREEN’s hardware can offer some seriously heavy-duty NVIDIA AI silicon. Smart homes are getting smarter, and that might just be a problem. While the idea of a more feature-reach, accessible, and proactive smart home sounds great on face value, the growing reliance of so many of these systems on cloud-based AI is making some shoppers think twice. UGREEN believes it might just have the solution in the form of some advanced smart home hubs. Ecosystems like Google Home tap into cloud-powered AI continually, from processing your voice input, to analyzing your Nest camera footage. Beyond obvious privacy considerations, there’s also the subscription cost to consider with the more advanced camera functionality, to say nothing of storage.

Plenty of us already know and love the convenience of magnetic Qi2 battery banks , ready to pop right on the back of compatible phones and cases. title: AWOL LuxVision brings 4K 120Hz and optical shift to UST projection
summary: High-refresh 4K gets a much more living-room-friendly setup.
body: Credit: AWOL TL;DR AWOL Vision has unveiled the LuxVision, its new flagship ultra-short-throw projector, at IFA 2026. AWOL says it’s the world’s first 4K 120Hz UST projector to also offer optical shift. The LuxVision is rated at 6,000 ISO lumens and launches around October from $6,499. Projectors are great if you want a ridiculously big picture, but setups with ceiling mounts or long cable runs, along with carefully calculated distances, aren’t exactly living-room friendly. Ultra-short-throw projectors solve much of that by sitting just inches from the wall, and AWOL Vision’s new LuxVision aims to eliminate another compromise by bringing true 4K 120Hz output and optical shift to the format. Unveiled at IFA 2026, AWOL bills the LuxVision as the world’s first 4K 120Hz ultra-short-throw projector with optical shift. That combination is the main selling point, as you get the smoother motion of a 120Hz display without giving up the living-room-friendly setup of a UST projector. At the same time, the optical shift gives you more freedom to position the image without compromising its 4K detail.

title: Nanoleaf wall panels now work in the Philips Hue app
summary: Philips Hue finally gets wall panels thanks to Nanoleaf.
body: Credit: Philips Hue TL;DR Signify has announced a partnership with Nanoleaf. The partnership will bring Nanoleaf Shapes into the Philips Hue ecosystem. You’ll need a Philips Hue Wall Light Module to integrate the panels into your setup. Ever since a slip-up revealed a hexagon-shaped panel icon in the Philips Hue app, we’ve been expecting a panel-related announcement. Initially, there was a belief that the company could launch its first-ever wall panel lights. However, a leak in late August revealed that the brand may instead integrate Nanoleaf panels via a new module . A recently published support page added more weight to this discovery. Now Philips Hue’s parent company has made it official. Amid all of the IFA 2026 news today, Signify announced a partnership between Philips Hue and Nanoleaf. That partnership will bring compatible Nanoleaf Shapes into the Hue ecosystem. Compatible panels include Nanoleaf Hexagons, Triangles, and Mini Triangles.

title: Digital Wellbeing could soon give you a weekly reality check

body: TL;DR Google is working on a Weekly wrap feature for Digital Wellbeing that could proactively recap your phone usage. Gemini Nano could turn your weekly screen-time data into personalized, contextual insights instead of just showing raw numbers. The feature is still in development, and there’s no guarantee Google will release it to users. Google’s Digital Wellbeing app is the place you’d go to know exactly how much time you’re spending on your phone . The catch, however, is that it’s largely a passive tool that you need to manually open and dig through. The tool doesn’t take a proactive approach, though that might soon change. Digital Wellbeing could soon add a new Weekly wrap feature that, exactly as it sounds, would give you a weekly recap of your phone usage.

Weather forecasting can be bang on the money, or infuriatingly inaccurate. Most of us have probably looked out the window at falling rain while our weather app confidently suggests we won’t get wet if we head out. Google is trying to close some of that gap with WeatherNext 3, its new AI weather model that should deliver more detailed, more frequently updated forecasts to services including Google Search, Gemini, and Maps. title: Smartphone prices may be soaring, but Americans are getting off easy
summary: US shoppers have less to worry about than most smartphone buyers.
body: TL;DR US smartphone prices rose just 5%, far less than the 15% global increase. New phones are getting pricier as memory costs squeeze manufacturers worldwide. Shoppers elsewhere face steeper hikes, making the US look surprisingly insulated. If you’ve been grumbling about the price of this year’s flagship phones , you’re not exactly wrong. Samsung, Google, and Motorola have all asked US shoppers to pay more for their latest flagships, with most of the increases landing around the $100 mark. But here’s the thing: It could be a whole lot worse. Counterpoint Research’s latest smartphone price tracker shows that global smartphone retail prices have climbed an average of 15% so far in 2026. More than 40% of smartphone models have seen price hikes this year, while new launches are coming in 25% more expensive than their year-ago counterparts.

body: بداية قوية لنجم الملكي أعلن ريال مدريد، مساء اليوم الخميس، الفائز بجائزة أفضل لاعب في الفريق عن شهر أغسطس/ آب، بعد انطلاقة قوية للموسم الجديد في الدوري الإسباني. وحسم النجم الفرنسي كيليان مبابي السباق لصالحه، متفوقًا على بقية لاعبي الفريق، وفي مقدمتهم الإنجليزي جود بيلينجهام، ليحصد أول جائزة شهرية له مع "الميرنجي" هذا الموسم. وجاء تتويج مبابي بعدما سجل 4 أهداف خلال أول 3 مباريات خاضها ريال مدريد في الدوري الإسباني، ولعب 270 دقيقة كاملة، كما سدد 18 كرة على مرمى المنافسين، إلى جانب إكمال 111 تمريرة لزملائه.   👏 ¡Enhorabuena, @KMbappe ! ✨ Jugador Cinco Estrellas · Agosto ⚽ @FutbolMahou pic.twitter.com/oXTE2VlKOU — Real Madrid C.F. body: خطف الأهلي، فوزًا قاتلًا أمام ضيفه سموحة، بهدف دون رد، مساء الخميس، في الجولة الثالثة من الدوري المصري الممتاز، على ستاد القاهرة الدولي. ولم يستطع لاعبو المارد الأحمر، فك شفرة دفاع سموحة، خلال الشوط الأول، الذي خرج بالتعادل السلبي. وفي الشوط الثاني، استمر طوفان هجوم الأهلي، حتى نجح المدافع ياسر إبراهيم في تسجيل هدف الفوز لأصحاب الأرض، من تسديدة قوية من خارج منطقة الجزاء، في الدقيقة 87. وأشهر الحكم أمين عمر، البطاقة الحمراء في وجه عمرو السيسي، لاعب سموحة، في الدقيقة 89. وارتفع رصيد الأهلي، مع مدربه المغربي الحسين عموتة، إلى 9 نقاط في وصافة البطولة، بفارق الأهداف عن بيراميدز، صاحب الصدارة، فيما ظل سموحة بنقطة واحدة، في المركز 18. وكان الأهلي قد بدأ مشواره في الدوري المصري الممتاز، بالفوز على الشرقية إنبي وزد، بنتيجة 3-2 و2-0 على الترتيب.        يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة بص شوف ياسر إبراهيم عملها ازاي🦅💪.. ياسر إبراهيم يسجل هدف رائع للأهلي في شباك سموحة ليتقدم المارد الأحمر🔴 pic.twitter.com/fpT1EYefcV — ON Sport (@ONTimeSports) September 3, 2026

title: Philips Hue is giving Bridge and Bridge Pro users a feature they’ve wanted for years

body: Credit: Signify TL;DR Philips Hue is launching several new smart light products. The company has also announced that it is previewing a backup and restore feature. Backup and restore will allow users of the Hue Bridge and Bridge Pro to back up their settings to the Hue cloud. Due to leaks, it’s been known for a few months now that Philips Hue would have some new products to show off later in the year. Some of those products include new Festavia lights and a camera for Hue Sync . Sure enough, the company has finally announced its next slate of lighting solutions. In addition to the new smart lights, Philips Hue is also giving users a highly requested feature. Backup and restore Starting with the new feature, Philips Hue announced that it is previewing a backup and restore function. With backup and restore, users of the Hue Bridge and Bridge Pro will be able to back up their settings to the Hue cloud. That means you’ll now be able to save settings, accessories, rooms, zones, scenes, automations, and more in case anything happens. This is something that many users have been wanting for years.

summary: Lenovo clearly believes size can change everything.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KLV4dFCEJ-E TL;DR Lenovo’s Project Swan is a 14-inch laptop concept with a rollable display that expands into a 17-inch, 16:9 screen. The idea combines the portability of a smaller laptop with extra screen space for multitasking, potentially replacing the need for a portable monitor. Project Swan is still a proof of concept, so there’s no pricing or release date, and questions around durability and battery life remain. Lenovo has never been particularly shy about making laptops do weird things. We’ve seen screens fold, twist, and even stretch vertically, and at IFA 2026 , the company is experimenting with another idea: What if your regular 14-inch laptop could suddenly give you a much wider screen when you need it? That’s the idea behind Project Swan, one of two Intel-powered laptop concepts Lenovo is showing off at IFA this year. title: This desktop robot companion is also an AI wearable you can wear around your neck
summary: The iKairos wants to watch you all day long.
body: TL;DR The Lingverse iKairos is a modular AI wearable that comes in the form of a desktop robot companion. It can also be detached and worn around the neck as an AI pendant. It will gather contextual data and surface relevant suggestions for users. Wearable AI pendants are nothing new, and neither are AI desktop companions . However, at IFA 2026, Singapore-based company Lingverse is showcasing a modular AI wearable that can both sit at your desk and hang around your neck. The company calls it iKairos, and its modular design lets it learn about the user’s life from different perspectives. At a desk, it will observe and interact with users like any other desktop AI robot. However, users can pop it out of its robot body and slot it into a necklace to take it with them on the go.

body: TL;DR Gmail, Docs, and Keep can now understand natural voice commands and turn them into useful actions. Docs Live can pull info from Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the web, while Keep Live organizes free-flowing thoughts into notes and lists. The new voice features are rolling out now to eligible Google AI subscribers, with Workspace support coming soon. Back at Google I/O, the company showed how Gemini could make Gmail, Docs, and Keep feel less like apps you operate and more like assistants you talk to. The company promised that these new voice-powered experiences would be available this summer, and after a few early glimpses , the wait is finally over. Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live are rolling out now, giving users new ways to get things done without reaching for the keyboard. Gmail Live is perhaps the most immediately useful of the three. Instead of digging through your inbox or remembering the right keywords, you can ask a question out loud. Gmail can connect information across emails to synthesize an answer. That could mean asking when your kid’s next school event is, checking an order update, or finding information buried across multiple messages.

New features include a built-in touchscreen display, dual Bluetooth headphone support, Nintendo Switch projection, and 2.5 hours of playback in ECO mode. We’ve learned to accept that in tech, anything portable will have compromises compared to its tethered counterpart — except phones , of course. Laptops are generally less powerful than desktops, wireless earbuds have the battery constraints that wired earbuds don’t, and projectors are no different. The smaller projectors get, the more features consumers tend to lose, such as brightness, resolution, battery life, and more. Aurzen knows that, and instead of trying to replace your living-room TV, the company’s new projector goes all in on making the big-screen experience as portable as possible.

The mission launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Roman pairs a large field of view with crisp infrared vision to explore vast swaths of the sky and probe deeply into cosmic history. This flagship mission will help astronomers explore dark matter, dark energy, and worlds outside of our solar system, known as exoplanets. title: Why modular design could be the next big shift for consumer exoskeletons
summary: At IFA 2026, Ascentiz is using its H, K, and H+K configuration to show how one wearable platform can support different forms of physical assistance.
body: Credit: Ascentiz In a young hardware category, progress is easy to measure by what can be seen: more torque, longer range, another powered joint. Consumer exoskeletons are now reaching a stage where the architecture behind those specifications may matter just as much. The question is no longer only how much assistance a device can deliver, but how many different needs the system can grow to support. That is the larger idea Ascentiz is bringing to IFA 2026. Its H hip module and K knee module address different movement demands and can be used independently. A new H+K configuration connects both through a hub, with BodyOS coordinating their work at the system level. Together, the three configurations make Ascentiz’s platform strategy tangible: specialized hardware on top of a shared Exo-Belt, communication architecture, and software foundation.

body: The Pixel lineup has visibly matured in the last few years. Gone are the days when Google would change its physical design every single year, making the camera bar a recognizable and stand-out feature. Google has made it easy to spot Pixels in a sea of iPhones at places like airports. And it’s the same tale with the software, which has become quite stable as a platform, and something you pick up a Pixel for. However, that stability comes along with decelerating growth. If you are lucky enough to experience a total eclipse somewhere quiet and close to nature, you may be able to notice unusual daytime animal behaviors . During totality, you may hear nighttime sounds like crickets and frogs and see fireflies . In the dark, most birds are quiet . body: A partial lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana on Aug. 28, 2026 NASA/Eric Bordelon On Aug. 28, 2026 (the evening of Aug. 27 in some time zones), the Moon passed into Earth’s shadow, creating a deep partial lunar eclipse . At the moment of greatest eclipse, 12:13 a.m. EDT, 96.3% of the Moon’s disk was immersed in Earth’s umbra—the central, darkest part of the shadow where sunlight is completely blocked. This stage of the eclipse was visible across much of the Americas (except Alaska and northwestern Canada), as well as western Europe and western Africa. This image of the eclipse was captured in southern Louisiana, home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility —the nation’s premier site for manufacturing and assembling large-scale space structures and systems, including the core stages of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket powering the Artemis program.
